title: Faithful Group Shapley Value

problems.title: The strict stability rate omits a logarithmic factor
problems.source_location: Proceedings Proposition 2, p. 7; separate supplement §A.6, p. 21.
claim: Proposition 2 gives a constant-factor second-order SGD rate under the stated polynomial step, batch and horizon scalings.
analysis: Let the common background records have feature zero, and choose four distinct added records with features \((1,1,0,0)\). The four size-\(N\) datasets contain respectively \(k=2,1,1,0\) unit-feature records. Use scalar loss \(\ell(w;z)=-a(z)w\), start \(w_0=0\), step \(N^{-1/4}/t\), batch size \(N\) and horizon \(N\). A bounded smooth utility can equal \(w^2\) on \([-2,2]\), extend as \(8-(4-|w|)^2\) for \(2<|w|<4\), and equal \(8\) outside; it has bounded derivative and Lipschitz derivative. Every reached iterate is below \(2\). Without replacement, \(w_T(k)=kN^{-5/4}H_N\), where \(H_N=\sum_{t\leq N}1/t\). Thus the four-utility difference is \(2N^{-5/2}H_N^2\). Independent with-replacement batches give \(2N^{-5/2}(H_N^2-H_N^{(2)}/N)\), with \(H_N^{(2)}=\sum_{t\leq N}t^{-2}\). Scaling by \(N^{5/2}\) diverges, contradicting the strict power-only bound under the stated regularity. This does not establish an optimal alternative rate.
result: The exponent-only bound needs qualification. This does not refute conditional faithfulness or prove an optimal alternative rate.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Retain the supplement’s capped exponent \(\nu_{\rm eff}=\min\{2\tau_1+\tau_2-1/2,1/2\}\) and its two-term bound, or explicitly account for the logarithmic factors under the example’s scaling.
problems.impact_rationale: The defect is a supporting quantitative stability refinement; the central conditional value characterization remains intact.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The benchmark estimator omits normalization factors
problems.source_location: Lemma 1/Eq. (8), p. 4; Theorem 2/Eq. (9), pp. 4–5; exp1_benchmark/estimators.py lines 343–405.
claim: The benchmark path estimates the defined FGSV by combining small- and large-cardinality branches.
analysis: For eight players and additive utility \(U(S)=|S\cap S_0|/8\), \(|S_0|=4\), exact group value is \(1/2\). The benchmark path omits the small-branch factor \(n/[s(n-s)]\) and large-branch factor \(n/(n-1)\), giving limiting value \(127/224\approx0.566964\). Additivity removes approximation remainder and within-stratum variation, so increasing samples does not remove that normalization bias. Other release paths partly include the factors.
result: The named estimator does not converge to the defined value on this additive control. Published benchmark exposure is unresolved.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Insert the missing cardinality factors while preserving the existing central-difference division by two. This restores this estimator’s algebraic correspondence, not a new benchmark result.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a public estimator defect with unresolved historical scientific impact.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
